name: Ghal Phaley
instructions: 1. Prepare the dough by kneading refined flour with water and a pinch of salt; let it rest for 30 minutes.
2. In a bowl, mix the minced meat with finely chopped onions, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, coriander, soy sauce, and pepper.
3. Roll small portions of dough into flat circles.
4. Place a spoonful of the meat mixture in the center, fold the dough into a half-moon shape, and seal the edges tightly by twisting or pressing with a fork.
5. Heat oil in a deep pan and fry the Ghal Phaley on medium heat until golden brown and the meat is thoroughly cooked inside.
6. Serve hot with spicy tomato chutney or a bowl of clear soup.
description: Ghal Phaley is a beloved snack in Sikkim with deep cultural roots in Tibetan cuisine. Often referred to as a Sikkimese meat pie, it is a staple comfort food frequently enjoyed at local eateries and street stalls, known for its crispy exterior and juicy, flavorful filling.
